faqs.q: What are the most famous Punjabi dishes?
faqs.a: Well-loved Punjabi dishes include sarson da saag with makki di roti, dal makhani, paneer butter masala, chole bhature, stuffed parathas such as aloo paratha, and tandoori breads like naan. Thick lassi and sweets made with ghee and jaggery, such as churi, are popular too.

faqs.q: What is the difference between dal makhani and ordinary dal?
faqs.a: Dal makhani is made with whole black lentils, often with some kidney beans, slow-cooked for a long time and finished with butter and cream, which makes it rich and creamy. Everyday dal is usually made with split lentils such as toor or moong and cooked more quickly with a simple tempering.

faqs.q: Why is sarson da saag eaten mainly in winter?
faqs.a: Sarson da saag is made from mustard greens, which grow in Punjab during the cooler months, so it is traditionally a winter dish. It is usually eaten with makki di roti made from maize flour, topped with butter or ghee, and is valued as a warming, filling meal in cold weather.

faqs.q: Is Punjabi food always heavy and rich?
faqs.a: No. Restaurant favourites such as dal makhani and butter masala dishes are rich because of butter and cream, but everyday Punjabi home food is often simpler, with dal, seasonal vegetables, roti, curd and salad. You can also ask for less butter or cream when ordering or cooking.
